author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: its date and description can be changed after the fact, updating the same visit in place without booking a second visit or removing the existing one. Reachable by URL only; cancellation stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for an existing visit (GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit) shows the visit form prefilled with that visit's current date and description, rendered from the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template with the visit exposed as the 'visit' model attribute.
Submitting a valid correction (POST to the same URL, description present and date later than today) updates that same visit's date and description in place and redirects to the owner detail page.
After a valid correction, the pet gains no additional visit record: the number of visits recorded against the pet is unchanged.
Submitting a correction with a blank description is refused, the description field is named as in error, and the form is redisplayed.
Submitting a correction with a date of today or earlier is refused, the date field is named as in error, and the form is redisplayed.
Validation rules match visit booking exactly: description required, date strictly later than today.
non_goals: Cancelling or removing a booked visit (NG-5 remainder; NG-4 deletion pattern)
Adding an edit link or any visible entry point to the correction form on the owner detail page in this round
notes: Narrows NG-5 per adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md. Reuse pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm unchanged. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions (narrowest reading taken, not waited on): (1) the reused template lists the pet's other visits including the one under correction; (2) the reused submit button reads 'Add Visit'. Both left as template-reuse-unchanged. Loading the existing visit by visitId is a mechanism detail for system-design-expert; Pet.java listed best-effort as the likely place to retrieve an existing visit. Note for a design-doc owner: the ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md needs a row for adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md (outside product-requirements-expert write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction reuses the create-and-update-through-OwnerRepository aggregate pattern the owner and pet edit flows already demonstrate (system-design.md Contracts: Owner is the sole write path for the owner-pet-visit graph; State Machine: workflows branch on BaseEntity.isNew to choose insert vs update). The only additions are thin, pattern-conforming extension points: a Pet.getVisit(Integer id) accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id) (Owner.java:117), and an optional visitId branch on VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:64). No new module, no lifecycle state, no new dependency, consistent with adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md. IDE oracle not consulted this run; the covering symbols (Owner.getPet(Integer), VisitController.loadPetWithVisit, Pet.getVisits) were confirmed by direct Read of the source files, a stronger basis than grep.
integration_points: Add Pet.getVisit(Integer id): iterate getVisits(), return the Visit whose non-null id equals the argument else null. Mirror Owner.getPet(Integer id) exactly (skip visits where isNew()). This is the retrieval-by-visitId path; Owner exposes no visit accessor, so retrieval belongs on the Pet aggregate that owns the visits collection.

Extend the @ModelAttribute("visit") method loadPetWithVisit with @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId. Branch: when visitId is null (the /visits/new route) keep the current behavior (new Visit(), pet.addVisit(visit), return it); when visitId is present (the /edit route) return pet.getVisit(visitId) WITHOUT calling addVisit, throwing IllegalArgumentException if null. Returning the existing persisted instance is what makes Spring bind the submitted date/description onto it in place.

Add the GET/POST handler pair for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. GET initEditVisitForm() returns "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm" (unchanged template, visit already prefilled by the model attribute). POST processEditVisitForm applies the SAME validation as processNewVisitForm (manual non-future date reject on field "date"; @NotBlank on description yields the "description" field error), then this.owners.save(owner) and redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. Do NOT call owner.addVisit in the edit POST.

REQ-VIS-003 mapping (VisitController and Pet now also serve REQ-VIS-003) is deferred to doc-sync after the code lands, keeping system-design.md code-derived rather than pre-recording state that does not yet exist.

patterns.description: Owner.getPet(Integer id) aggregate-by-id accessor to mirror as Pet.getVisit(Integer id)
processNewVisitForm validation + save-through-OwnerRepository pattern to mirror for the edit POST

risks.risk: Route collision or wrong in-place semantics: if the model attribute adds a new Visit on the edit path, or the edit POST calls owner.addVisit, the pet gains a duplicate visit (breaks AC3).
risks.mitigation: The edit branch returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and never calls addVisit; save cascades an UPDATE because the loaded Visit already has an id. Test processEditVisitFormAddsNoNewVisit asserts pet.getVisits().size() is unchanged. Paths /visits/new and /visits/{visitId}/edit are structurally distinct, so no Spring MVC mapping ambiguity.

risks.risk: Reused template posts to the wrong URL, so the edit form submits to /new.
risks.mitigation: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html binds th:object=${visit} and posts to the current request URI; verify by Read that the form action is not hard-coded to the /new path. PRD fixed template-reuse-unchanged, so a template edit is out of scope for this slice — surface as a consultation if the action is hard-coded.

notes: Verdict minor: single existing pattern with two thin extension points (a Pet accessor and an optional path-variable branch), no new architectural ground. ADR index row for adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction.md added to docs/adr/README.md in this dispatch. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Pet.java changes are the getVisit accessor only; the retrieve-vs-add distinction is a controller concern realized via that accessor, not a persistence-mapping change.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: IDOR/path-variable scoping is correct: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner->pet->visit through the aggregate (owners.findById(ownerId), owner.getPet(petId), pet.getVisit(visitId)); pet.getVisit matches only non-new visits with equal id within THIS pet, so a visitId outside the {ownerId,petId} hierarchy returns null and yields IllegalArgumentException rather than leaking or mutating another pet/owner visit (VisitController.java:63-90, Pet.java:91-101).

Mass-assignment guarded: @InitBinder disallows id and *.id (VisitController.java:51-54), so the in-place edit cannot repoint the persisted visit id; binding modifies the loaded Visit instance in place. The @ModelAttribute Owner bind+save mirrors the pre-existing processNewVisitForm pattern and introduces no new over-binding surface.

No injection: uses OwnerRepository (Spring Data, no query-string construction); reused Thymeleaf createOrUpdateVisitForm template is unchanged and auto-escapes the user-supplied description, so no stored/reflected XSS is introduced.

Data-integrity/in-place update is sound: edit POST omits addVisit and saves through the Owner aggregate so the visit id drives a cascade UPDATE; validation matches booking (non-future date reject on field date, @NotBlank on description). Tests processEditVisitFormAddsNoNewVisit and processEditVisitFormSuccessUpdatesVisitInPlace confirm no duplicate record.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods are named in the implementation-mirroring school (e.g. initEditVisitFormPrefillsCurrentDateAndDescription) rather than the BDD school required for tests written after 2026-07-31. The brief (docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming) requires the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming for all new tests in this slice. Suggested renames: theEditVisitFormShouldPrefillCurrentDateAndDescription, theEditVisitFormShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlace, theEditVisitFormShouldAddNoNewVisitRecord, theEditVisitFormShouldRejectABlankDescription, theEditVisitFormShouldRejectANonFutureDate.
findings.fix: Rename the five methods to the BDD school: theEditVisitFormShouldPrefillCurrentDateAndDescription, theEditVisitFormShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlace, theEditVisitFormShouldAddNoNewVisitRecord, theEditVisitFormShouldRejectABlankDescription, theEditVisitFormShouldRejectANonFutureDate.

findings.description: The @BeforeEach init() method constructs Owner, Pet, and Visit directly via new. The brief (docs/testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction) requires all construction in tests written or modified after 2026-07-31 to be behind factory methods. This slice extended init() to add the existingVisit setup (lines 73-77), making the direct-construction a current violation, not pre-existing debt alone.
findings.fix: Introduce factory methods (e.g. createOwnerWithPet(), createFutureVisit(int daysAhead, String description)) and replace the direct new Owner(), new Pet(), new Visit() calls in init() with those factories. Existing pre-slice constants (TEST_OWNER_ID, TEST_PET_ID) are pre-existing debt; the new constructions added by this slice must be moved behind factories.

findings.description: TEST_VISIT_ID = 1 is a new constant introduced by this slice. Its specific value has no bearing on the test outcome — the visit ID in the fixture could be any integer. Per the three-tier naming convention (docs/testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming Convention), irrelevant fixture values must carry a SOME_ or ANY_ prefix. The pre-existing TEST_OWNER_ID and TEST_PET_ID are pre-existing debt; the new constant must conform.
findings.fix: Rename TEST_VISIT_ID to SOME_VISIT_ID (value unchanged at 1) and update all references in the five new test methods.

approved_aspects: All six acceptance criteria are covered: prefill of date and description (AC1), in-place update with redirect to /owners/{ownerId} (AC2), visit count unchanged assertion (AC3), blank description rejection naming the description field (AC4), non-future date rejection naming the date field with typeMismatch.visitDate error code (AC5), validation rules matching booking (AC6)

processEditVisitFormAddsNoNewVisit genuinely asserts visit count: it captures pet.getVisits().size() before the POST and asserts hasSize(visitCountBefore) after — a substantive behavioral assertion, not a proxy

processEditVisitFormSuccessUpdatesVisitInPlace retrieves the visit after the POST via pet.getVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID) and asserts its mutated description and date — directly verifying in-place semantics, not just the redirect
The boundary for non-future date uses LocalDate.now() (today is invalid, tomorrow is valid) — exactly matching AC5 and the booking validation
No new mock classes introduced; the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository is pre-existing and tolerated per the brief (§ Mocking Policy: mock-framework stubs on the existing suite may stay)
Four-phase structure is clean: blank lines separate arrange from act from assert; no narration comments
Redirect target redirect:/owners/{ownerId} verified in the success test
Template name pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm verified in both GET and error-path tests
AssertJ fluent assertions used for standalone post-request assertions; MockMvc Hamcrest matchers used where MockMvc requires them — both are correct in context
Tests are independent with no shared mutable state between test methods
All five tests pass without failures or skips

author: change-grader
summary: grade in-place edit of a booked visit date and description

blast_radius.note: Contained to the owner package (Pet accessor plus two controller mappings) and its test, with matching docs; six files, 20 hunks, no sensitive paths, no cross-stack reach.

semantic_surprise.note: The edit path reuses the existing @ModelAttribute loader: visitId present routes to pet.getVisit(id) and binds the form onto that same instance, so save(owner) updates in place with no second record; date validation mirrors the new-visit path exactly, and disallowed id binding is preserved. Nothing behaves beyond what the diff describes.

test_adequacy.note: Five new tests assert real outcomes: prefill of current date/description, in-place field update via getVisit, unchanged visit count, blank-description rejection, and non-future-date rejection with the exact error code. They exercise the changed boundary rather than restate it.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers final-approve with empty findings; the two changes_requested rounds (test naming/factory, PRD design-rationale link) were autofix/fixable items fully resolved and re-approved clean, not lingering reservations.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries; the diff matches REQ-VIS-003 exactly (correct date and description in place, URL-only, no cancellation), and the narrowing ADR plus PRD rows document the deliberate NG-5 narrowing.

rationale: All five facets clear. The in-place edit reuses the proven booking pattern with no behavioral surprise, tests assert the real boundaries, reviewers approve cleanly, and the change stays within its narrowed scope. Confirm the diff and merge; a fast read suffices.
